S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).

subtypes.Animal Type: Marked fear of animals or insects like dogs, bees, snakes, or spiders.
subtypes.Natural Environment Type: Marked fear of the natural environment like storms, heights, water, or the dark.
subtypes.Blood-Injection-Injury Type: Marked fear of seeing blood, receiving injections, or medical procedures.
subtypes.Situational Type: Marked fear of specific situations like airplanes, elevators, tunnels, bridges, or enclosed spaces.
subtypes.Other Type: Marked fear of other situations like choking, vomiting, loud sounds, or costumed characters.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Anticipatory Anxiety: Strong anxiety triggered just by thinking about the possibility of encountering the phobic object.
subtypes.Immediate Panic Response: Overwhelming fear erupting immediately upon facing the phobic object.
subtypes.Physiological Panic Symptoms: Intense physical reactions such as heart palpitations, shortness of breath, sweating, or trembling.
subtypes.Freezing: Feeling paralyzed or unable to move due to extreme fear.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Active Avoidance: Intentionally and completely staying away from contact with the phobic object or situation.
subtypes.Functional Impairment due to Avoidance: Accepting severe restrictions on daily life, job, or social activities to avoid the phobic object.
subtypes.Enduring with Distress: Forcing oneself to endure the situation while experiencing intense fear and anxiety because it cannot be avoided.
subtypes.Reliance on Safety Signals: Barely enduring the exposure by relying on a companion or safety object.

symptom.disease_info: Specific Phobia is characterized by a persistent, excessive fear of a clearly defined object or situation (e.g., animals, heights, flying, injections) that almost invariably triggers anxiety and leads to avoidance or intense distress. The fear is out of proportion to the actual danger and has lasted at least six months, causing significant interference in social, occupational, or daily functioning. Onset often occurs in childhood or adolescence but phobias can emerge or worsen in adulthood, especially after a distressing encounter with the feared stimulus or during periods of heightened stress. It is distinguished from other anxiety disorders by the narrow focus of the fear and the absence of broader worries, obsessions, or panic attacks in varied contexts.

patient.stressor: James’s specific fear emerged about two and a half years after his wife’s death, when his adult children began encouraging him to fly to California and the East Coast more often so he wouldn’t be alone for long stretches. He had flown occasionally when younger, but a particularly turbulent flight to visit a cousin shortly after his wife’s funeral left him feeling unusually shaken and acutely aware of his age and frailty, and he quietly decided to avoid flying again. Over time, that decision hardened into a rigid refusal to consider any air travel, even for family milestones such as a granddaughter’s graduation, causing growing conflict with his children and limiting his ability to pursue long-dreamed-of trips to places like Kyoto and Tuscany. When he found himself making elaborate excuses to avoid even entering the small local airport for an art exhibit and noticed how much his world had shrunk despite otherwise good health, he agreed at his daughter’s urging to see a psychiatrist at the VA-affiliated clinic to address this entrenched fear.
patient.chief_complaint: “I go to great lengths to avoid getting on an airplane, even when it means missing important family events.”

S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).
S062.manifestation: Ever since that rough flight after my wife’s funeral, the idea of being sealed in a metal tube at 30,000 feet with no way out just terrifies me in a way that I know doesn’t quite make sense, but it feels like I’d be signing my own death warrant if I got on a plane again at my age.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.
S063.manifestation: If one of the kids even mentions buying a ticket, my heart starts pounding, my hands go clammy, and I picture the plane dropping out of the sky so vividly that I have to change the subject or get up and walk around.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.
S064.manifestation: I’ve turned down graduations, holidays, and even a free trip to Italy, and I make up excuses about my back or my budget, because the truth is I’ll do almost anything not to step foot on an airplane, even walking out of that art exhibit at the little airport when I realized I’d have to pass too close to the gates.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: Because I refuse to fly, I’ve missed my granddaughter’s graduation and several family gatherings on the coasts, and I’ve given up on the trips abroad I’d always planned for retirement, which has left me feeling more isolated and regretful as the years go by.
add_requirements.duration: This fear around flying has really taken hold and stayed with me for a little over two years now, ever since that turbulent flight I took not long after my wife’s funeral.
